fact: NAM-CSIRT's 2025 landscape report says that in the absence of a cybersecurity law in Namibia it looks to the government to expedite the Cybercrime Bill and related regulations, and recommends finalising and enacting the Cybercrime, Data Protection and CII regulations; the document carries no issue date, so its published date is used.

NAMPA reports that the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology consulted stakeholders from Kavango East, Kavango West and Zambezi at Rundu on the proposed cybersecurity and cybercrime bill, the Namibia Cybercrime Bill, which is not yet law.
The Speaker of the National Assembly said Namibia is finalising a Cybercrime Bill to address digital threats.
New Era reports the ICT ministry is finalising key legislation, including the Cybercrime Bill, to address legal gaps.
The Brief names a Cybercrime Bill that aims to counter technology-enabled and AI-related threats, as of January 2026.

The Windhoek Observer, citing the Ministry of Finance's 2026/27 budget estimates, reports that drafting of Namibia's Cybercrime Bill is complete and it is expected to go to Parliament in March 2026 after a validation workshop.
A draft Cybercrime Bill was presented at a MICT public stakeholders' engagement in Windhoek, and the article says Namibia has no legislation yet directly governing cyber criminal behaviour.
The Namibian reports ICT Minister Emma Theofelus saying the drafting of the cybercrime bill is still underway and making progress, delayed by a lack of local cyberlaw expertise.
CRAN says Namibia lacks dedicated cybercrime and data protection legislation.
